content.value_statement: Security teams need a clear way to map attack paths and defense gaps. This skill builds structured attack trees with metrics, mitigations, and export templates.
actual_capabilities: Defines OR, AND, and leaf node structures for attack trees.
Annotates attack leaves with cost, skill, time, and detection risk.
Identifies easiest, cheapest, and stealthiest paths in a tree.
Exports attack trees as JSON, Mermaid, or PlantUML examples.
Prioritizes mitigations by attack path coverage.
limitations: Requires an authorized system scope and clear attacker goal.
Does not validate real exploit feasibility or vulnerability presence.
Provides templates and analysis guidance, not live scanning.
May require expert review for complex systems and regulated environments.

use_cases.title: Map Product Attack Paths
use_cases.description: Create a scoped attack tree for a product feature and identify the most important defense gaps.

use_cases.title: Plan Control Investments
use_cases.description: Compare mitigation options by path coverage, residual risk, and implementation impact.

use_cases.title: Explain Risk Clearly
use_cases.description: Convert complex attack scenarios into diagrams and summaries for technical and business stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Attack Tree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner threat modeling for a known system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a high-level attack tree for [system]. Scope is [scope], root goal is [goal], and audience is [audience]. Include OR and AND nodes, leaf attacks, mitigations, and assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Risk Attributes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis of an existing tree.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this attack tree: [tree]. Add cost, skill, time, and detection attributes to each leaf. Highlight the easiest and highest priority paths.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Mitigation Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced defense planning for open paths.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this attack tree and existing controls: [controls], identify open paths. Rank mitigations by path coverage, implementation effort, and residual risk.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Stakeholder Briefing
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this scoped attack tree for [asset]. Produce a concise executive summary, technical findings, unresolved assumptions, and a mitigation roadmap for [timeframe].

output_examples.input: Model account takeover risks for a consumer web application.
output: Root goal: take over a user account.
Main branches: steal credentials, bypass authentication, and abuse account recovery.
Priority controls: MFA, rate limits, session protections, and support verification.

output_examples.input: Find defense gaps in a payment workflow attack tree.
output: Open paths remain for weak approval controls and delayed anomaly detection.
The highest coverage mitigation is stronger transaction approval with audit alerts.
Residual risk should be reviewed with fraud, engineering, and compliance teams.

output_examples.input: Prepare an executive summary from a completed attack tree.
output_examples.output: The model shows three realistic paths to the root goal. Two are reduced by existing controls, while one requires stronger identity verification and monitoring.

best_practices: Confirm authorization, assets, and scope before modeling any attack path.
Use high-level leaf descriptions unless sensitive detail is required for defense work.
Review high-impact paths with security, engineering, and business owners.
anti_patterns: Building trees for systems outside your authorization.
Treating attack trees as proof that a vulnerability exists.
Sharing sensitive exploit detail with audiences that do not need it.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps create structured attack trees for authorized threat modeling and defense planning.

faq.question: Does it run scans or exploit systems?
faq.answer: No. It provides modeling guidance, analysis templates, and diagram formats.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the system scope, attacker goal, assets, assumptions, and known controls.

faq.question: Can it help with executive communication?
faq.answer: Yes. It can summarize attack paths, defense gaps, and mitigation priorities in plain language.

faq.question: Can it produce diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes Mermaid and PlantUML export patterns for attack tree diagrams.

faq.question: Is it suitable for red team planning?
faq.answer: It can support authorized planning, scoping, and communication. It should not be used outside approved work.
